stem: A skier descends a frictionless slope, dropping 10 m vertically. Using energy conservation, what is the skier's speed at the bottom (g = 10 m/s²)?

choices.text: 80 J, calculated as W = Fd = 20 × 4, ignoring the angle
40 J, calculated using sin 30° instead of cos 30°
approximately 69 J, calculated as W = Fd cos θ = 20 × 4 × cos 30° ≈ 69 J
0 J, because only the horizontal component of velocity matters

explanation.short: W = Fd cos θ. The force component along the direction of motion is F cos θ. W = 20 × 4 × cos 30° = 80 × 0.866 ≈ 69 J.
explanation.detailed: W = Fd cos θ. The force component along the direction of motion is F cos θ. W = 20 × 4 × cos 30° = 80 × 0.866 ≈ 69 J. This item tests MCAT-style mechanistic reasoning.
explanation.why_correct: C is correct: approximately 69 J, calculated as W = Fd cos θ = 20 × 4 × cos 30° ≈ 69 J.

wrong_answer_explanations.A: W = Fd only when force is parallel to displacement; the angle must be accounted for with cos θ
wrong_answer_explanations.B: The component of force along the displacement uses cos θ, not sin θ; sin 30° = 0.5 gives 40 J, which is incorrect
wrong_answer_explanations.C: This is the correct answer.
wrong_answer_explanations.D: Work is force times displacement in the direction of force regardless of velocity; 0 J is only correct when force is perpendicular to displacement

explanation.high_yield_takeaway: W = Fd cos θ. Perpendicular force does zero work. Parallel force does maximal work.
explanation.common_trap: Using the full force magnitude without the cosine factor; always project force onto displacement.
explanation.how_to_think: Predict the expected relationship before reading choices, then eliminate those that reverse or overstate it.

stem: Three resistors of 6 Ω, 3 Ω, and 2 Ω are connected in parallel. What is the equivalent resistance?

choices.text: 11 Ω, calculated by summing resistances as if in series
2 Ω, by taking only the smallest resistance
3 Ω, by averaging the three resistances

explanation.short: Parallel: 1/Req = Σ(1/Ri). Series: Req = ΣRi. Parallel resistance is always less than the smallest individual resistance.
explanation.detailed: Parallel: 1/Req = Σ(1/Ri). Series: Req = ΣRi. Parallel resistance is always less than the smallest individual resistance. This item tests MCAT-style mechanistic reasoning.
explanation.why_correct: D is correct: 1 Ω, calculated from 1/Req = 1/6 + 1/3 + 1/2 = 1/6 + 2/6 + 3/6 = 6/6 = 1.

wrong_answer_explanations.A: Adding resistances directly applies to series circuits; parallel resistors always yield a lower equivalent resistance than any single branch
wrong_answer_explanations.B: The equivalent parallel resistance is always less than the smallest branch resistor; taking the minimum directly ignores the other paths
wrong_answer_explanations.C: Averaging has no basis in circuit analysis; the reciprocal formula must be applied
wrong_answer_explanations.D: This is the correct answer.

explanation.high_yield_takeaway: Parallel: 1/Req = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + …. Result is always lower than smallest branch.
explanation.common_trap: Adding parallel resistors as if in series (the most common error); parallel adds conductances, not resistances.
explanation.how_to_think: Predict the expected relationship before reading choices, then eliminate those that reverse or overstate it.

stem: Blood flows through a wide aorta into a narrower artery. According to the continuity equation, how does velocity change?

choices.text: resistance increases by a factor of 16, because Poiseuille resistance is inversely proportional to radius to the fourth power
resistance increases by a factor of 4, because area decreases by a factor of 4 when radius halves
resistance decreases because a narrower vessel allows faster flow
resistance increases by a factor of 2, because halving the radius doubles the resistance

explanation.short: Poiseuille: R = 8ηL/(πr⁴). Halving r increases R by (1/0.5)⁴ = 2⁴ = 16. Small changes in vessel radius have dramatic effects on resistance.
explanation.detailed: Poiseuille: R = 8ηL/(πr⁴). Halving r increases R by (1/0.5)⁴ = 2⁴ = 16. Small changes in vessel radius have dramatic effects on resistance. This item tests MCAT-style mechanistic reasoning.
explanation.why_correct: A is correct: resistance increases by a factor of 16, because Poiseuille resistance is inversely proportional to radius to the fourth power.

wrong_answer_explanations.A: This is the correct answer.
wrong_answer_explanations.B: The r⁴ relationship is steeper than proportional to area; a factor of 4 would apply to a simple area-based formula
wrong_answer_explanations.C: Resistance increases in a narrower vessel; while velocity can increase (continuity), the driving pressure required rises dramatically
wrong_answer_explanations.D: Resistance scales with r⁻⁴, not r⁻¹; halving r raises resistance by 2⁴ = 16, not 2

explanation.high_yield_takeaway: Poiseuille: R ∝ 1/r⁴. Halving radius → 16× resistance. Continuity: A₁v₁ = A₂v₂.
explanation.common_trap: Using r² (area) instead of r⁴ in Poiseuille's law; the fourth-power dependence is the high-yield fact here.
explanation.how_to_think: Predict the expected relationship before reading choices, then eliminate those that reverse or overstate it.

stem: A converging lens with focal length 10 cm forms an image of an object placed 30 cm from the lens. Which description of the image is correct?

choices.text: no image forms because the object is beyond the focal length
a virtual, upright image located 15 cm from the lens on the same side as the object
a real, upright image located 30 cm from the lens
a real, inverted, and diminished image located 15 cm from the lens on the far side

explanation.short: 1/f = 1/do + 1/di → 1/10 = 1/30 + 1/di → 1/di = 1/10 − 1/30 = 2/30 → di = 15 cm. Positive di = real and inverted.
explanation.detailed: 1/f = 1/do + 1/di → 1/10 = 1/30 + 1/di → 1/di = 1/10 − 1/30 = 2/30 → di = 15 cm. Positive di = real and inverted. This item tests MCAT-style mechanistic reasoning.
explanation.why_correct: D is correct: a real, inverted, and diminished image located 15 cm from the lens on the far side.

wrong_answer_explanations.A: Objects beyond the focal length always produce real images; objects inside the focal length produce virtual images
wrong_answer_explanations.B: Virtual, upright images form only when the object is inside the focal length; here object distance (30 cm) > f (10 cm), so a real image forms
wrong_answer_explanations.C: Real images formed by converging lenses are always inverted; a real upright image is impossible with a single converging lens
wrong_answer_explanations.D: This is the correct answer.

explanation.high_yield_takeaway: Thin lens: 1/f = 1/do + 1/di. Positive di → real, inverted image. Negative di → virtual, upright.
explanation.common_trap: Assuming objects beyond 2f always produce diminished images; use the lens equation to calculate rather than guess.
explanation.how_to_think: Predict the expected relationship before reading choices, then eliminate those that reverse or overstate it.

stem: Two waves of equal amplitude and frequency interfere. One wave is shifted by half a wavelength relative to the other. What is the resultant amplitude?

choices.text: constructive interference: approaching sources always amplify sound
the Doppler effect: the observer perceives higher frequency because successive wave crests arrive more frequently as the source approaches
diffraction: sound bends around the observer causing frequency increase
resonance: the truck's frequency matches the observer's natural frequency

explanation.short: Doppler effect: when source and observer approach, observed frequency f' = f(v+vo)/(v−vs). Moving source approaching → f' > f; receding → f' < f.
explanation.detailed: Doppler effect: when source and observer approach, observed frequency f' = f(v+vo)/(v−vs). Moving source approaching → f' > f; receding → f' < f. This item tests MCAT-style mechanistic reasoning.
explanation.why_correct: B is correct: the Doppler effect: the observer perceives higher frequency because successive wave crests arrive more frequently as the source approaches.

wrong_answer_explanations.A: Constructive interference involves overlapping waves in space, not a moving source; the effect disappears when the truck passes
wrong_answer_explanations.B: This is the correct answer.
wrong_answer_explanations.C: Diffraction is bending of waves around obstacles; it does not shift the perceived frequency
wrong_answer_explanations.D: Resonance requires matching natural frequencies of a resonating body; it does not cause a frequency shift tied to source motion

explanation.high_yield_takeaway: Doppler: approaching source → higher observed frequency. Receding → lower. Half-wavelength shift → destructive interference (amplitude = 0).
explanation.common_trap: Confusing Doppler (frequency shift from motion) with changes in amplitude or resonance phenomena.
explanation.how_to_think: Predict the expected relationship before reading choices, then eliminate those that reverse or overstate it.

wrong_answer_explanations.D: A 100:1 ratio gives pH = pKa + 2; the two-unit shift is double what the question specifies

explanation.high_yield_takeaway: Each pH unit from pKa corresponds to a 10-fold change in [A−]/[HA].

stem: Nitrogen and hydrogen gases react to form ammonia. Adding more nitrogen to the equilibrium mixture at constant volume and temperature shifts the reaction in which direction?

explanation.short: Le Chatelier's principle: a system at equilibrium responds to oppose any imposed change. Compression increases pressure, so the reaction shifts toward the side with fewer gas moles to relieve it.

explanation.high_yield_takeaway: Le Chatelier: predict the direction that reduces the applied stress. Keq changes only with temperature.

stem: The Nernst equation predicts how cell potential changes as a reaction proceeds. At equilibrium, which value does Q equal?

choices.text: E is undefined when Q departs from 1
E = E°cell because Q < 1 has no effect until equilibrium
E < E°cell because non-standard conditions always reduce the driving force
E > E°cell because when Q < 1 the reaction quotient term (−RT/nF × ln Q) is positive, adding to E°

explanation.short: Nernst equation: E = E° − (RT/nF)ln Q. When Q < 1, ln Q < 0, so the subtracted term becomes negative, raising E above E°.
explanation.detailed: Nernst equation: E = E° − (RT/nF)ln Q. When Q < 1, ln Q < 0, so the subtracted term becomes negative, raising E above E°. This item tests MCAT-style mechanistic reasoning.
explanation.why_correct: D is correct: E > E°cell because when Q < 1 the reaction quotient term (−RT/nF × ln Q) is positive, adding to E°.

wrong_answer_explanations.A: The Nernst equation applies at any Q; it is well-defined for all positive Q values
wrong_answer_explanations.B: Q < 1 means products are low relative to reactants, increasing the driving force and raising E above E°
wrong_answer_explanations.C: Non-standard E can be higher than E° when Q < 1; the assumption that it is always lower ignores the log term's sign
wrong_answer_explanations.D: This is the correct answer.

explanation.high_yield_takeaway: Q < 1 → E > E°. Q > 1 → E < E°. Q = Keq → E = 0 (equilibrium).
explanation.common_trap: Students assume non-standard always means lower potential; direction depends on whether Q < 1 or Q > 1.
explanation.how_to_think: Predict the expected relationship before reading choices, then eliminate those that reverse or overstate it.

stem: A mixture of H2 (M = 2) and O2 (M = 32) effuses through a small opening. Which gas effuses faster and by what factor?

choices.text: both gases effuse at the same rate because temperature determines kinetic energy equally
H2 effuses twice as fast because its molar mass is half that of O2
H2 effuses 4 times faster than O2 because rate is inversely proportional to the square root of molar mass
O2 effuses faster because it has more mass and therefore more momentum

explanation.short: Graham's law: rate ∝ 1/√M. Rate(H2)/Rate(O2) = √(32/2) = √16 = 4.
explanation.detailed: Graham's law: rate ∝ 1/√M. Rate(H2)/Rate(O2) = √(32/2) = √16 = 4. This item tests MCAT-style mechanistic reasoning.
explanation.why_correct: C is correct: H2 effuses 4 times faster than O2 because rate is inversely proportional to the square root of molar mass.

wrong_answer_explanations.A: Temperature equalizes average kinetic energy but not speed; lighter molecules move faster at the same KE
wrong_answer_explanations.B: H2/O2 molar mass ratio is 1/16, so rate ratio = √16 = 4, not 2; square root is required
wrong_answer_explanations.C: This is the correct answer.
wrong_answer_explanations.D: Graham's law gives rate ∝ 1/√M; heavier gas is slower, not faster, regardless of momentum

explanation.high_yield_takeaway: Graham's law: ratio of rates = square root of the inverse molar mass ratio.
explanation.common_trap: Students use the molar mass ratio directly rather than its square root.
explanation.how_to_think: Predict the expected relationship before reading choices, then eliminate those that reverse or overstate it.

stem: Red blood cells placed in a 0.9% NaCl solution maintain their normal shape. When transferred to distilled water, they swell and lyse. Which colligative property explains lysis?

choices.text: NaCl solution has a higher boiling point because it dissociates into two ions (Na+ and Cl−), doubling the effective particle concentration
NaCl has a lower boiling point because ionic solutes disrupt hydrogen bonding more than covalent solutes
glucose has a higher boiling point because larger molecules create more surface interactions with water
both solutions have identical boiling points because molality determines boiling point elevation regardless of solute identity

explanation.short: ΔTb = iKbm. NaCl (i ≈ 2) doubles the effective molality relative to glucose (i = 1), producing twice the boiling point elevation.
explanation.detailed: ΔTb = iKbm. NaCl (i ≈ 2) doubles the effective molality relative to glucose (i = 1), producing twice the boiling point elevation. This item tests MCAT-style mechanistic reasoning.
explanation.why_correct: A is correct: NaCl solution has a higher boiling point because it dissociates into two ions (Na+ and Cl−), doubling the effective particle concentration.

wrong_answer_explanations.A: This is the correct answer.

wrong_answer_explanations.C: Boiling point elevation is a colligative property depending on particle number, not molecular size or polarity
wrong_answer_explanations.D: The van't Hoff factor i accounts for dissociation; NaCl has i = 2, glucose i = 1, so they differ at equal molality

explanation.how_to_think: Predict the expected relationship before reading choices, then eliminate those that reverse or overstate it.

stem: A primary alkyl bromide reacts with sodium cyanide (strong nucleophile) in acetone. Which mechanism and stereochemical outcome are most expected?

choices.text: SN2 with inversion of configuration, because the primary substrate is unhindered and the strong nucleophile performs backside attack
E2 elimination because cyanide is too bulky to reach the backside
SN1 with racemization, because the primary substrate forms a stable primary carbocation that is attacked from both faces
No reaction because primary substrates are too stable for nucleophilic substitution

explanation.short: SN2: strong nucleophile + primary (or methyl) substrate + polar aprotic solvent → inversion. SN1: weak nucleophile or solvolysis + tertiary substrate + polar protic solvent → racemization.
explanation.detailed: SN2: strong nucleophile + primary (or methyl) substrate + polar aprotic solvent → inversion. SN1: weak nucleophile or solvolysis + tertiary substrate + polar protic solvent → racemization. This item tests MCAT-style mechanistic reasoning.
explanation.why_correct: A is correct: SN2 with inversion of configuration, because the primary substrate is unhindered and the strong nucleophile performs backside attack.

wrong_answer_explanations.A: This is the correct answer.
wrong_answer_explanations.B: Cyanide is a linear, compact anion and is not sterically hindered; bulky bases favor elimination but cyanide is not bulky
wrong_answer_explanations.C: Primary carbocations are highly unstable and do not form under normal conditions; SN1 requires at least secondary (preferably tertiary) substrates
wrong_answer_explanations.D: Primary substrates are among the most reactive in SN2 due to minimal steric hindrance; they do react readily

explanation.high_yield_takeaway: SN2: primary, strong Nu, polar aprotic, inversion. SN1: tertiary, weak Nu, polar protic, racemization.
explanation.common_trap: Students default to SN1 for any substrate; remember primary substrates cannot form stable carbocations.
explanation.how_to_think: Predict the expected relationship before reading choices, then eliminate those that reverse or overstate it.

stem: An aldehyde is treated with excess sodium borohydride (NaBH4) in methanol. What is the primary product?

choices.text: a primary alcohol (from aldehyde reduction) because NaBH4 delivers hydride to the carbonyl carbon
a secondary alcohol, because NaBH4 always adds two carbons to the carbonyl
an acetal, because methanol attacks the carbonyl under all conditions
a carboxylic acid, because NaBH4 oxidizes aldehydes in the presence of base

explanation.short: NaBH4 donates hydride (H−) to the electrophilic carbonyl carbon. Aldehydes (RCHO) → primary alcohols (RCH2OH). Ketones (RCOR′) → secondary alcohols (RCHOHR′).
explanation.detailed: NaBH4 donates hydride (H−) to the electrophilic carbonyl carbon. Aldehydes (RCHO) → primary alcohols (RCH2OH). Ketones (RCOR′) → secondary alcohols (RCHOHR′). This item tests MCAT-style mechanistic reasoning.
explanation.why_correct: A is correct: a primary alcohol (from aldehyde reduction) because NaBH4 delivers hydride to the carbonyl carbon.

wrong_answer_explanations.A: This is the correct answer.
wrong_answer_explanations.B: Hydride addition replaces C=O with C–OH; no carbons are added—only hydrogen. Aldehydes give primary alcohols, ketones give secondary
wrong_answer_explanations.C: Acetal formation requires an acid catalyst and two equivalents of alcohol; NaBH4 reduction proceeds differently
wrong_answer_explanations.D: NaBH4 is a reducing agent that delivers H−; it does not oxidize and does not produce carboxylic acids

explanation.high_yield_takeaway: NaBH4/LiAlH4 reduce carbonyls. Aldehyde → 1° alcohol; ketone → 2° alcohol; ester/acid → 1° alcohol (LiAlH4 only).
explanation.common_trap: Confusing reduction product class: aldehydes give primary, ketones give secondary—not both secondary.
explanation.how_to_think: Predict the expected relationship before reading choices, then eliminate those that reverse or overstate it.

stem: Two compounds share the same molecular formula and sequence of bonds but differ in the spatial arrangement of groups around one chiral center. They are non-superimposable mirror images. How are they related?

they are constitutional isomers because they differ in the spatial arrangement of atoms
they are diastereomers because having two chiral centers always creates diastereomers
they are enantiomers because they are non-superimposable mirror images differing at every chiral center

explanation.short: Enantiomers: non-superimposable mirror images. Diastereomers: stereoisomers that are NOT mirror images (differ at some but not all chiral centers). Meso compounds are achiral despite having stereocenters.
explanation.detailed: Enantiomers: non-superimposable mirror images. Diastereomers: stereoisomers that are NOT mirror images (differ at some but not all chiral centers). Meso compounds are achiral despite having stereocenters. This item tests MCAT-style mechanistic reasoning.

wrong_answer_explanations.C: Diastereomers differ at some but not all chiral centers; the mirror image relationship that is non-superimposable defines enantiomers

explanation.high_yield_takeaway: Enantiomers = mirror images that are non-superimposable. Diastereomers = stereoisomers that are not mirror images.
explanation.common_trap: Thinking that any molecule with two stereocenters must form diastereomers; the relationship depends on which centers differ.

stem: An IR spectrum shows a broad absorption centered near 3300 cm−1 and a sharp absorption at 1715 cm−1. Which functional groups are most consistent with these peaks?

an alkyne C≡C (~2100–2260 cm−1) and an alcohol O–H (~3300 cm−1)
an aldehyde C–H (two weak peaks ~2700–2850 cm−1) and a C–O ether stretch (~1100 cm−1)
an alcohol O–H (broad 3200–3550 cm−1) and a carbonyl C=O (sharp ~1715 cm−1)

wrong_answer_explanations.D: This is the correct answer.

explanation.high_yield_takeaway: W = Fd cos θ. Perpendicular force does zero work. Parallel force does maximal work.
explanation.common_trap: Using the full force magnitude without the cosine factor; always project force onto displacement.

stem: Three resistors of 6 Ω, 3 Ω, and 2 Ω are connected in parallel. What is the equivalent resistance?

3 Ω, by averaging the three resistances

passage.text: A study examines fluids using a controlled animal model. Investigators are specifically interested in distinguishing undefined from related phenomena.

stem: Blood flows through a wide aorta into a narrower artery. According to the continuity equation, how does velocity change?

choices.text: resistance increases by a factor of 4, because area decreases by a factor of 4 when radius halves
resistance increases by a factor of 2, because halving the radius doubles the resistance
resistance decreases because a narrower vessel allows faster flow
resistance increases by a factor of 16, because Poiseuille resistance is inversely proportional to radius to the fourth power

explanation.short: Poiseuille: R = 8ηL/(πr⁴). Halving r increases R by (1/0.5)⁴ = 2⁴ = 16. Small changes in vessel radius have dramatic effects on resistance.
explanation.detailed: Poiseuille: R = 8ηL/(πr⁴). Halving r increases R by (1/0.5)⁴ = 2⁴ = 16. Small changes in vessel radius have dramatic effects on resistance. This item tests MCAT-style mechanistic reasoning.
explanation.why_correct: D is correct: resistance increases by a factor of 16, because Poiseuille resistance is inversely proportional to radius to the fourth power.

wrong_answer_explanations.A: The r⁴ relationship is steeper than proportional to area; a factor of 4 would apply to a simple area-based formula
wrong_answer_explanations.B: Resistance scales with r⁻⁴, not r⁻¹; halving r raises resistance by 2⁴ = 16, not 2
wrong_answer_explanations.C: Resistance increases in a narrower vessel; while velocity can increase (continuity), the driving pressure required rises dramatically
wrong_answer_explanations.D: This is the correct answer.

explanation.high_yield_takeaway: Poiseuille: R ∝ 1/r⁴. Halving radius → 16× resistance. Continuity: A₁v₁ = A₂v₂.
explanation.common_trap: Using r² (area) instead of r⁴ in Poiseuille's law; the fourth-power dependence is the high-yield fact here.
explanation.how_to_think: Predict the expected relationship before reading choices, then eliminate those that reverse or overstate it.

passage.title: Optics Scenario
passage.text: A study examines optics using a randomized clinical study. Investigators are specifically interested in distinguishing undefined from related phenomena.

stem: A converging lens with focal length 10 cm forms an image of an object placed 30 cm from the lens. Which description of the image is correct?

choices.text: a virtual, upright image located 15 cm from the lens on the same side as the object
a real, upright image located 30 cm from the lens
no image forms because the object is beyond the focal length
a real, inverted, and diminished image located 15 cm from the lens on the far side

explanation.short: 1/f = 1/do + 1/di → 1/10 = 1/30 + 1/di → 1/di = 1/10 − 1/30 = 2/30 → di = 15 cm. Positive di = real and inverted.
explanation.detailed: 1/f = 1/do + 1/di → 1/10 = 1/30 + 1/di → 1/di = 1/10 − 1/30 = 2/30 → di = 15 cm. Positive di = real and inverted. This item tests MCAT-style mechanistic reasoning.
explanation.why_correct: D is correct: a real, inverted, and diminished image located 15 cm from the lens on the far side.

wrong_answer_explanations.A: Virtual, upright images form only when the object is inside the focal length; here object distance (30 cm) > f (10 cm), so a real image forms
wrong_answer_explanations.B: Real images formed by converging lenses are always inverted; a real upright image is impossible with a single converging lens
wrong_answer_explanations.C: Objects beyond the focal length always produce real images; objects inside the focal length produce virtual images
wrong_answer_explanations.D: This is the correct answer.

explanation.high_yield_takeaway: Thin lens: 1/f = 1/do + 1/di. Positive di → real, inverted image. Negative di → virtual, upright.
explanation.common_trap: Assuming objects beyond 2f always produce diminished images; use the lens equation to calculate rather than guess.
explanation.how_to_think: Predict the expected relationship before reading choices, then eliminate those that reverse or overstate it.

passage.title: Waves Scenario
passage.text: A study examines waves using a computational pharmacokinetic model. Investigators are specifically interested in distinguishing undefined from related phenomena.

stem: Two waves of equal amplitude and frequency interfere. One wave is shifted by half a wavelength relative to the other. What is the resultant amplitude?

choices.text: constructive interference: approaching sources always amplify sound
resonance: the truck's frequency matches the observer's natural frequency
diffraction: sound bends around the observer causing frequency increase
the Doppler effect: the observer perceives higher frequency because successive wave crests arrive more frequently as the source approaches

explanation.short: Doppler effect: when source and observer approach, observed frequency f' = f(v+vo)/(v−vs). Moving source approaching → f' > f; receding → f' < f.
explanation.detailed: Doppler effect: when source and observer approach, observed frequency f' = f(v+vo)/(v−vs). Moving source approaching → f' > f; receding → f' < f. This item tests MCAT-style mechanistic reasoning.
explanation.why_correct: D is correct: the Doppler effect: the observer perceives higher frequency because successive wave crests arrive more frequently as the source approaches.

wrong_answer_explanations.A: Constructive interference involves overlapping waves in space, not a moving source; the effect disappears when the truck passes
wrong_answer_explanations.B: Resonance requires matching natural frequencies of a resonating body; it does not cause a frequency shift tied to source motion
wrong_answer_explanations.C: Diffraction is bending of waves around obstacles; it does not shift the perceived frequency
wrong_answer_explanations.D: This is the correct answer.

explanation.high_yield_takeaway: Doppler: approaching source → higher observed frequency. Receding → lower. Half-wavelength shift → destructive interference (amplitude = 0).
explanation.common_trap: Confusing Doppler (frequency shift from motion) with changes in amplitude or resonance phenomena.
explanation.how_to_think: Predict the expected relationship before reading choices, then eliminate those that reverse or overstate it.

passage.title: Structural basis for water permeability and ion exclusion in human aquaporin-1 determined by cryo-electron microscopy
passage.text: Structural basis for water permeability and ion exclusion in human aquaporin-1 determined by cryo-electron microscopy. Background: Aquaporin-1 (AQP1) facilitates osmotic water transport with high selectivity, excluding ions and protons by mechanisms not fully resolved. Methods: Human AQP1 in lipid nanodiscs was determined at 1.9 Å resolution by cryo-EM; molecular dynamics simulations modeled water permeation. Results: The selectivity filter pore narrows to 3 Å, lined by Asn76, Arg195, and His180. Water traverses in single file, reorienting midway to prevent proton conductance via the Grotthuss mechanism.

stem: A buffer prepared from acetic acid (pKa 4.76) and sodium acetate has pH 5.76. Which ratio of [acetate]/[acetic acid] satisfies the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation?

choices.text: 1:10 (acid to base), because the ratio appears inverted when the log term is misread
100:1, because the pH difference from pKa is mistakenly doubled
10:1 (conjugate base to acid), because pH exceeds pKa by exactly one unit and log(10) = 1
1:1, because equal concentrations always produce a pH equal to the pKa

explanation.short: pH = pKa + log([A−]/[HA]). A pH one unit above pKa requires [A−]/[HA] = 10¹ = 10.
explanation.detailed: pH = pKa + log([A−]/[HA]). A pH one unit above pKa requires [A−]/[HA] = 10¹ = 10. This item tests MCAT-style mechanistic reasoning.
explanation.why_correct: C is correct: 10:1 (conjugate base to acid), because pH exceeds pKa by exactly one unit and log(10) = 1.

wrong_answer_explanations.A: A 1:10 ratio gives pH = pKa − 1, not pKa + 1; inverting the base/acid direction reverses the sign of the log term
wrong_answer_explanations.B: A 100:1 ratio gives pH = pKa + 2; the two-unit shift is double what the question specifies
wrong_answer_explanations.C: This is the correct answer.
wrong_answer_explanations.D: Equal concentrations give pH = pKa (log 1 = 0); this ignores the one-unit pH elevation specified

explanation.high_yield_takeaway: Each pH unit from pKa corresponds to a 10-fold change in [A−]/[HA].
explanation.common_trap: Confusing acid/base direction in the ratio flips the sign and gives the mirror-image wrong answer.
explanation.how_to_think: Predict the expected relationship before reading choices, then eliminate those that reverse or overstate it.

stem: A researcher titrates a weak acid with NaOH. At the half-equivalence point, which observation is most expected?

choices.text: the half-equivalence point maximizes ionic strength rather than buffering ability
buffer capacity is maximal when [HA] = [A−] because both components are available to neutralize added acid or base
buffers work by preventing any ionization of water near physiological pH
buffer capacity is maximal at pH extremes because the excess form absorbs all perturbation

wrong_answer_explanations.D: Buffer capacity is actually lowest at pH extremes, where one component is nearly depleted

explanation.high_yield_takeaway: Maximum buffer capacity occurs at pH = pKa (half-equivalence point).
explanation.common_trap: Students often think diluting a buffer maintains the same capacity; capacity falls with concentration even if pH is unchanged.

passage.title: Thermodynamics Scenario
passage.text: A study examines thermodynamics using a randomized clinical study. Investigators are specifically interested in distinguishing undefined from related phenomena.

stem: A reaction has ΔH = −80 kJ/mol and ΔS = −200 J/(mol·K). At what temperature does the reaction shift from spontaneous to non-spontaneous?

choices.text: ΔH positive and ΔS negative, which is never spontaneous at any temperature
ΔH negative and ΔS negative; the unfavorable −TΔS term (positive) overtakes ΔH at high temperature
ΔH positive and ΔS positive, which becomes spontaneous at high temperature, not low
ΔH negative and ΔS positive, which is spontaneous at all temperatures

explanation.short: ΔG = ΔH − TΔS. When both terms are negative, ΔG < 0 at low T but the +TΔS term eventually dominates as T rises, making ΔG > 0.
explanation.detailed: ΔG = ΔH − TΔS. When both terms are negative, ΔG < 0 at low T but the +TΔS term eventually dominates as T rises, making ΔG > 0. This item tests MCAT-style mechanistic reasoning.
explanation.why_correct: B is correct: ΔH negative and ΔS negative; the unfavorable −TΔS term (positive) overtakes ΔH at high temperature.

wrong_answer_explanations.A: ΔH+ / ΔS− gives ΔG positive at all temperatures; it cannot be spontaneous at any temperature
wrong_answer_explanations.B: This is the correct answer.
wrong_answer_explanations.C: ΔH+ / ΔS+ reactions become spontaneous as T rises (high-T favorable), the opposite of what's described
wrong_answer_explanations.D: ΔH− / ΔS+ gives ΔG negative at all temperatures; this cannot shift from spontaneous to non-spontaneous

explanation.high_yield_takeaway: Memorize the four ΔH/ΔS sign combinations and their temperature dependence.
explanation.common_trap: Confusing which sign combination is 'always spontaneous' vs 'temperature-dependent' is the most common error.
explanation.how_to_think: Predict the expected relationship before reading choices, then eliminate those that reverse or overstate it.

stem: Nitrogen and hydrogen gases react to form ammonia. Adding more nitrogen to the equilibrium mixture at constant volume and temperature shifts the reaction in which direction?

choices.text: the equilibrium shifts toward reactants regardless of the mole ratio of gases
the equilibrium shifts toward the product side (fewer gas moles) to reduce pressure, consistent with Le Chatelier's principle
the equilibrium constant Keq increases because higher pressure favors product formation
no shift occurs because Keq depends only on temperature, so concentrations are unaffected

explanation.short: Le Chatelier's principle: a system at equilibrium responds to oppose any imposed change. Compression increases pressure, so the reaction shifts toward the side with fewer gas moles to relieve it.
explanation.detailed: Le Chatelier's principle: a system at equilibrium responds to oppose any imposed change. Compression increases pressure, so the reaction shifts toward the side with fewer gas moles to relieve it. This item tests MCAT-style mechanistic reasoning.
explanation.why_correct: B is correct: the equilibrium shifts toward the product side (fewer gas moles) to reduce pressure, consistent with Le Chatelier's principle.

wrong_answer_explanations.A: Le Chatelier predicts the system opposes the disturbance; if products have fewer gas moles, compression favors products, not reactants
wrong_answer_explanations.B: This is the correct answer.
wrong_answer_explanations.C: Keq is a constant at fixed temperature; pressure changes shift the reaction position but never change Keq
wrong_answer_explanations.D: Concentration and pressure changes do shift the equilibrium position; it is Keq that remains constant, not the concentrations

explanation.high_yield_takeaway: Le Chatelier: predict the direction that reduces the applied stress. Keq changes only with temperature.
explanation.common_trap: Students confuse 'Keq does not change' with 'nothing happens.' Reactant and product concentrations shift even though Keq stays the same.
explanation.how_to_think: Predict the expected relationship before reading choices, then eliminate those that reverse or overstate it.

stem: A galvanic cell uses zinc and copper half-cells. Which statement correctly identifies the anode?

choices.text: the anode is whichever electrode has the higher concentration of metal ions
the copper electrode is the anode because copper has a higher reduction potential and accepts electrons
in a galvanic cell the anode is the positive terminal, so it is where reduction occurs
the zinc electrode is the anode because zinc is oxidized (loses electrons), which drives the spontaneous cell

explanation.short: Oxidation at the Anode (An Ox), Reduction at the Cathode (Red Cat). In a galvanic cell, the more easily oxidized metal becomes the anode. Zinc (E° = −0.76 V) is more easily oxidized than copper (E° = +0.34 V).
explanation.detailed: Oxidation at the Anode (An Ox), Reduction at the Cathode (Red Cat). In a galvanic cell, the more easily oxidized metal becomes the anode. Zinc (E° = −0.76 V) is more easily oxidized than copper (E° = +0.34 V). This item tests MCAT-style mechanistic reasoning.
explanation.why_correct: D is correct: the zinc electrode is the anode because zinc is oxidized (loses electrons), which drives the spontaneous cell.

wrong_answer_explanations.A: Electrode identity (anode/cathode) is determined by the half-reaction type (oxidation/reduction), not ion concentration
wrong_answer_explanations.B: A higher reduction potential means copper is preferentially reduced at the cathode, not oxidized at the anode
wrong_answer_explanations.C: In a galvanic cell the anode is negative (source of electrons flowing out); reduction occurs at the cathode, not the anode
wrong_answer_explanations.D: This is the correct answer.

explanation.high_yield_takeaway: An Ox, Red Cat. Galvanic anode is negative; electrolytic anode is positive (connected to +).
explanation.common_trap: Students flip anode/cathode sign in galvanic vs electrolytic cells. In both, oxidation is always at the anode.
explanation.how_to_think: Predict the expected relationship before reading choices, then eliminate those that reverse or overstate it.

stem: The Nernst equation predicts how cell potential changes as a reaction proceeds. At equilibrium, which value does Q equal?

choices.text: E > E°cell because when Q < 1 the reaction quotient term (−RT/nF × ln Q) is positive, adding to E°
E = E°cell because Q < 1 has no effect until equilibrium
E < E°cell because non-standard conditions always reduce the driving force
E is undefined when Q departs from 1

explanation.short: Nernst equation: E = E° − (RT/nF)ln Q. When Q < 1, ln Q < 0, so the subtracted term becomes negative, raising E above E°.
explanation.detailed: Nernst equation: E = E° − (RT/nF)ln Q. When Q < 1, ln Q < 0, so the subtracted term becomes negative, raising E above E°. This item tests MCAT-style mechanistic reasoning.
explanation.why_correct: A is correct: E > E°cell because when Q < 1 the reaction quotient term (−RT/nF × ln Q) is positive, adding to E°.

wrong_answer_explanations.A: This is the correct answer.
wrong_answer_explanations.B: Q < 1 means products are low relative to reactants, increasing the driving force and raising E above E°
wrong_answer_explanations.C: Non-standard E can be higher than E° when Q < 1; the assumption that it is always lower ignores the log term's sign
wrong_answer_explanations.D: The Nernst equation applies at any Q; it is well-defined for all positive Q values

explanation.high_yield_takeaway: Q < 1 → E > E°. Q > 1 → E < E°. Q = Keq → E = 0 (equilibrium).
explanation.common_trap: Students assume non-standard always means lower potential; direction depends on whether Q < 1 or Q > 1.
explanation.how_to_think: Predict the expected relationship before reading choices, then eliminate those that reverse or overstate it.

stem: A mixture of H2 (M = 2) and O2 (M = 32) effuses through a small opening. Which gas effuses faster and by what factor?

choices.text: H2 effuses twice as fast because its molar mass is half that of O2
both gases effuse at the same rate because temperature determines kinetic energy equally
O2 effuses faster because it has more mass and therefore more momentum
H2 effuses 4 times faster than O2 because rate is inversely proportional to the square root of molar mass

explanation.short: Graham's law: rate ∝ 1/√M. Rate(H2)/Rate(O2) = √(32/2) = √16 = 4.
explanation.detailed: Graham's law: rate ∝ 1/√M. Rate(H2)/Rate(O2) = √(32/2) = √16 = 4. This item tests MCAT-style mechanistic reasoning.
explanation.why_correct: D is correct: H2 effuses 4 times faster than O2 because rate is inversely proportional to the square root of molar mass.

wrong_answer_explanations.A: H2/O2 molar mass ratio is 1/16, so rate ratio = √16 = 4, not 2; square root is required
wrong_answer_explanations.B: Temperature equalizes average kinetic energy but not speed; lighter molecules move faster at the same KE
wrong_answer_explanations.C: Graham's law gives rate ∝ 1/√M; heavier gas is slower, not faster, regardless of momentum
wrong_answer_explanations.D: This is the correct answer.

explanation.high_yield_takeaway: Graham's law: ratio of rates = square root of the inverse molar mass ratio.
explanation.common_trap: Students use the molar mass ratio directly rather than its square root.
explanation.how_to_think: Predict the expected relationship before reading choices, then eliminate those that reverse or overstate it.

stem: Red blood cells placed in a 0.9% NaCl solution maintain their normal shape. When transferred to distilled water, they swell and lyse. Which colligative property explains lysis?

choices.text: NaCl solution has a higher boiling point because it dissociates into two ions (Na+ and Cl−), doubling the effective particle concentration
glucose has a higher boiling point because larger molecules create more surface interactions with water
both solutions have identical boiling points because molality determines boiling point elevation regardless of solute identity
NaCl has a lower boiling point because ionic solutes disrupt hydrogen bonding more than covalent solutes

explanation.short: ΔTb = iKbm. NaCl (i ≈ 2) doubles the effective molality relative to glucose (i = 1), producing twice the boiling point elevation.
explanation.detailed: ΔTb = iKbm. NaCl (i ≈ 2) doubles the effective molality relative to glucose (i = 1), producing twice the boiling point elevation. This item tests MCAT-style mechanistic reasoning.
explanation.why_correct: A is correct: NaCl solution has a higher boiling point because it dissociates into two ions (Na+ and Cl−), doubling the effective particle concentration.

wrong_answer_explanations.A: This is the correct answer.
wrong_answer_explanations.B: Boiling point elevation is a colligative property depending on particle number, not molecular size or polarity
wrong_answer_explanations.C: The van't Hoff factor i accounts for dissociation; NaCl has i = 2, glucose i = 1, so they differ at equal molality
wrong_answer_explanations.D: Both ionic and covalent solutes elevate boiling point; NaCl elevates it more because it produces more particles per formula unit

explanation.high_yield_takeaway: Colligative properties depend on particle count, not identity. Ionic solutes dissociate, multiplying their effect.
explanation.common_trap: Forgetting the van't Hoff factor i and treating NaCl as a non-electrolyte is the classic trap.
explanation.how_to_think: Predict the expected relationship before reading choices, then eliminate those that reverse or overstate it.

passage.title: Intensive versus standard blood pressure control and cardiovascular outcomes: results from the CLARITY-HTN randomized trial
passage.text: Intensive versus standard blood pressure control and cardiovascular outcomes: results from the CLARITY-HTN randomized trial. Background: Whether targeting systolic BP below 120 mmHg reduces cardiovascular events more than standard targets (<140 mmHg) without unacceptable adverse effects is debated. Methods: CLARITY-HTN randomized 9,361 high-risk hypertensive adults 1:1 to intensive or standard treatment for a median 4.2 years. Primary outcome: MACE (stroke, MI, cardiovascular death). Results: MACE occurred in 5.1% vs 7.8% (HR 0.64, 95% CI 0.54–0.76, p<0.001). Stroke risk was reduced 41%.

stem: The control condition in this experiment serves primarily to:

choices.text: the study provides evidence that the independent variable produces the observed change in the outcome, consistent with the proposed mechanism described in the abstract
the lack of a negative control means any observed effect could be due to handling alone
the results cannot be generalized because the study used a non-human model system
the correlational design proves a direct causal relationship between the variables measured

explanation.short: Research passage questions require identifying what the data support versus what they prove, and distinguishing study limitations from study invalidation.
explanation.detailed: Research passage questions require identifying what the data support versus what they prove, and distinguishing study limitations from study invalidation. This item tests MCAT-style mechanistic reasoning.
explanation.why_correct: A is correct: the study provides evidence that the independent variable produces the observed change in the outcome, consistent with the proposed mechanism described in the abstract.

wrong_answer_explanations.A: This is the correct answer.
wrong_answer_explanations.B: The study may have a negative control not explicitly mentioned; this extreme inference goes beyond the information given
wrong_answer_explanations.C: Model systems have limitations but provide mechanistic evidence; failure to generalize is a concern, not an absolute disqualifier
wrong_answer_explanations.D: Even well-designed studies cannot prove causation from correlation; the word 'proves' is too strong and is a classic wrong-answer signal on the MCAT

explanation.high_yield_takeaway: Evidence 'supports' a conclusion; it rarely 'proves' one. Always ask: what does the control group tell you?
explanation.common_trap: Selecting answers that use absolute language ('proves,' 'cannot,' 'always') when the data only support a probabilistic conclusion.
explanation.how_to_think: Predict the expected relationship before reading choices, then eliminate those that reverse or overstate it.

stem: A primary alkyl bromide reacts with sodium cyanide (strong nucleophile) in acetone. Which mechanism and stereochemical outcome are most expected?

choices.text: E2 elimination because cyanide is too bulky to reach the backside
SN1 with racemization, because the primary substrate forms a stable primary carbocation that is attacked from both faces
SN2 with inversion of configuration, because the primary substrate is unhindered and the strong nucleophile performs backside attack
No reaction because primary substrates are too stable for nucleophilic substitution

explanation.short: SN2: strong nucleophile + primary (or methyl) substrate + polar aprotic solvent → inversion. SN1: weak nucleophile or solvolysis + tertiary substrate + polar protic solvent → racemization.
explanation.detailed: SN2: strong nucleophile + primary (or methyl) substrate + polar aprotic solvent → inversion. SN1: weak nucleophile or solvolysis + tertiary substrate + polar protic solvent → racemization. This item tests MCAT-style mechanistic reasoning.
explanation.why_correct: C is correct: SN2 with inversion of configuration, because the primary substrate is unhindered and the strong nucleophile performs backside attack.

wrong_answer_explanations.A: Cyanide is a linear, compact anion and is not sterically hindered; bulky bases favor elimination but cyanide is not bulky
wrong_answer_explanations.B: Primary carbocations are highly unstable and do not form under normal conditions; SN1 requires at least secondary (preferably tertiary) substrates
wrong_answer_explanations.C: This is the correct answer.
wrong_answer_explanations.D: Primary substrates are among the most reactive in SN2 due to minimal steric hindrance; they do react readily

explanation.high_yield_takeaway: SN2: primary, strong Nu, polar aprotic, inversion. SN1: tertiary, weak Nu, polar protic, racemization.
explanation.common_trap: Students default to SN1 for any substrate; remember primary substrates cannot form stable carbocations.
explanation.how_to_think: Predict the expected relationship before reading choices, then eliminate those that reverse or overstate it.

passage.title: Nucleophilic Substitution Scenario
passage.text: A study examines nucleophilic substitution using a controlled animal model. Investigators are specifically interested in distinguishing undefined from related phenomena.

stem: A researcher treats a secondary substrate with a weak nucleophile in a polar protic solvent at room temperature. What is the most likely mechanism?

choices.text: SN2 substitution because methoxide is also a nucleophile and secondary substrates always substitute
SN1 because secondary substrates always ionize to carbocations in polar solvents
E2 elimination product because a strong base at high temperature with a secondary substrate favors elimination over substitution
No reaction because elimination requires a tertiary substrate

explanation.short: Strong base + heat → elimination (E2). At room temperature with a good nucleophile → SN2. Secondary substrates are at the crossroads; temperature and base strength decide.
explanation.detailed: Strong base + heat → elimination (E2). At room temperature with a good nucleophile → SN2. Secondary substrates are at the crossroads; temperature and base strength decide. This item tests MCAT-style mechanistic reasoning.
explanation.why_correct: C is correct: E2 elimination product because a strong base at high temperature with a secondary substrate favors elimination over substitution.

wrong_answer_explanations.A: Methoxide is both a strong base and nucleophile; high temperature and secondary substrate tip the competition toward E2 elimination
wrong_answer_explanations.B: Secondary substrates can do SN2, but the combination of strong base + heat + secondary strongly favors E2
wrong_answer_explanations.C: This is the correct answer.
wrong_answer_explanations.D: E2 elimination occurs at primary and secondary substrates; tertiary substrates favor E1 or E2 but are not the only option

explanation.high_yield_takeaway: Heat + strong base + secondary → E2. Room temp + good nucleophile + secondary → SN2.
explanation.common_trap: Students forget that the same reagent (e.g., NaOEt) can act as nucleophile or base; context (temperature, substrate) determines which role dominates.
explanation.how_to_think: Predict the expected relationship before reading choices, then eliminate those that reverse or overstate it.

passage.title: Carbonyl Chemistry Scenario
passage.text: A study examines carbonyl chemistry using a randomized clinical study. Investigators are specifically interested in distinguishing undefined from related phenomena.

stem: An aldehyde is treated with excess sodium borohydride (NaBH4) in methanol. What is the primary product?

choices.text: a primary alcohol (from aldehyde reduction) because NaBH4 delivers hydride to the carbonyl carbon
an acetal, because methanol attacks the carbonyl under all conditions
a carboxylic acid, because NaBH4 oxidizes aldehydes in the presence of base
a secondary alcohol, because NaBH4 always adds two carbons to the carbonyl

explanation.short: NaBH4 donates hydride (H−) to the electrophilic carbonyl carbon. Aldehydes (RCHO) → primary alcohols (RCH2OH). Ketones (RCOR′) → secondary alcohols (RCHOHR′).
explanation.detailed: NaBH4 donates hydride (H−) to the electrophilic carbonyl carbon. Aldehydes (RCHO) → primary alcohols (RCH2OH). Ketones (RCOR′) → secondary alcohols (RCHOHR′). This item tests MCAT-style mechanistic reasoning.
explanation.why_correct: A is correct: a primary alcohol (from aldehyde reduction) because NaBH4 delivers hydride to the carbonyl carbon.

wrong_answer_explanations.A: This is the correct answer.
wrong_answer_explanations.B: Acetal formation requires an acid catalyst and two equivalents of alcohol; NaBH4 reduction proceeds differently
wrong_answer_explanations.C: NaBH4 is a reducing agent that delivers H−; it does not oxidize and does not produce carboxylic acids
wrong_answer_explanations.D: Hydride addition replaces C=O with C–OH; no carbons are added—only hydrogen. Aldehydes give primary alcohols, ketones give secondary

explanation.high_yield_takeaway: NaBH4/LiAlH4 reduce carbonyls. Aldehyde → 1° alcohol; ketone → 2° alcohol; ester/acid → 1° alcohol (LiAlH4 only).
explanation.common_trap: Confusing reduction product class: aldehydes give primary, ketones give secondary—not both secondary.
explanation.how_to_think: Predict the expected relationship before reading choices, then eliminate those that reverse or overstate it.

passage.title: Stereochemistry Scenario
passage.text: A study examines stereochemistry using a computational pharmacokinetic model. Investigators are specifically interested in distinguishing undefined from related phenomena.

stem: Two compounds share the same molecular formula and sequence of bonds but differ in the spatial arrangement of groups around one chiral center. They are non-superimposable mirror images. How are they related?

choices.text: they are enantiomers because they are non-superimposable mirror images differing at every chiral center
they are identical compounds viewed from different angles
they are constitutional isomers because they differ in the spatial arrangement of atoms
they are diastereomers because having two chiral centers always creates diastereomers

explanation.short: Enantiomers: non-superimposable mirror images. Diastereomers: stereoisomers that are NOT mirror images (differ at some but not all chiral centers). Meso compounds are achiral despite having stereocenters.
explanation.detailed: Enantiomers: non-superimposable mirror images. Diastereomers: stereoisomers that are NOT mirror images (differ at some but not all chiral centers). Meso compounds are achiral despite having stereocenters. This item tests MCAT-style mechanistic reasoning.
explanation.why_correct: A is correct: they are enantiomers because they are non-superimposable mirror images differing at every chiral center.

wrong_answer_explanations.A: This is the correct answer.
wrong_answer_explanations.B: Non-superimposability is the test for enantiomers; if the two structures were identical, one could be superimposed on the other
wrong_answer_explanations.C: Constitutional isomers differ in connectivity; stereoisomers share the same connectivity but differ in spatial arrangement
wrong_answer_explanations.D: Diastereomers differ at some but not all chiral centers; the mirror image relationship that is non-superimposable defines enantiomers

explanation.high_yield_takeaway: Enantiomers = mirror images that are non-superimposable. Diastereomers = stereoisomers that are not mirror images.
explanation.common_trap: Thinking that any molecule with two stereocenters must form diastereomers; the relationship depends on which centers differ.
explanation.how_to_think: Predict the expected relationship before reading choices, then eliminate those that reverse or overstate it.

stem: An IR spectrum shows a broad absorption centered near 3300 cm−1 and a sharp absorption at 1715 cm−1. Which functional groups are most consistent with these peaks?

choices.text: an alcohol O–H (broad 3200–3550 cm−1) and a carbonyl C=O (sharp ~1715 cm−1)
an amine N–H (sharp doublet ~3300–3500 cm−1) and an alkene C=C (~1640 cm−1)
an aldehyde C–H (two weak peaks ~2700–2850 cm−1) and a C–O ether stretch (~1100 cm−1)
an alkyne C≡C (~2100–2260 cm−1) and an alcohol O–H (~3300 cm−1)

explanation.short: Broad O–H: 3200–3550 cm−1 (alcohol) or 2500–3300 cm−1 (carboxylic acid). Carbonyl C=O: ~1715 cm−1 (ketone/acid), ~1735 cm−1 (ester), ~1670 cm−1 (amide). Aldehyde C–H: ~2720 and 2820 cm−1.
explanation.detailed: Broad O–H: 3200–3550 cm−1 (alcohol) or 2500–3300 cm−1 (carboxylic acid). Carbonyl C=O: ~1715 cm−1 (ketone/acid), ~1735 cm−1 (ester), ~1670 cm−1 (amide). Aldehyde C–H: ~2720 and 2820 cm−1. This item tests MCAT-style mechanistic reasoning.
explanation.why_correct: A is correct: an alcohol O–H (broad 3200–3550 cm−1) and a carbonyl C=O (sharp ~1715 cm−1).

wrong_answer_explanations.A: This is the correct answer.
wrong_answer_explanations.B: Amine N–H appears as a sharp doublet (primary) or singlet (secondary), not a broad single peak; alkene C=C absorbs ~1640 cm−1, not 1715 cm−1
wrong_answer_explanations.C: Aldehyde C–H appears as two weak peaks near 2700–2850 cm−1, not a broad 3300 cm−1 absorption; ether C–O is ~1100 cm−1, not 1715
wrong_answer_explanations.D: Alkyne triple bond absorbs ~2100–2260 cm−1; the 1715 cm−1 carbonyl is inconsistent with this pairing

explanation.high_yield_takeaway: Broad O–H ~3300 = alcohol. Carbonyl ~1715 = ketone or acid. Aldehyde: two weak C–H peaks ~2700–2850.
explanation.common_trap: Mistaking the aldehyde C–H doublet for alcohol O–H; aldehyde peak is weak and appears as two peaks, not a broad hump.
explanation.how_to_think: Predict the expected relationship before reading choices, then eliminate those that reverse or overstate it.

passage.title: Work and Energy Scenario
passage.text: A study examines work and energy using a controlled animal model. Investigators are specifically interested in distinguishing undefined from related phenomena.

stem: A skier descends a frictionless slope, dropping 10 m vertically. Using energy conservation, what is the skier's speed at the bottom (g = 10 m/s²)?

choices.text: 0 J, because only the horizontal component of velocity matters
approximately 69 J, calculated as W = Fd cos θ = 20 × 4 × cos 30° ≈ 69 J
80 J, calculated as W = Fd = 20 × 4, ignoring the angle
40 J, calculated using sin 30° instead of cos 30°

explanation.short: W = Fd cos θ. The force component along the direction of motion is F cos θ. W = 20 × 4 × cos 30° = 80 × 0.866 ≈ 69 J.
explanation.detailed: W = Fd cos θ. The force component along the direction of motion is F cos θ. W = 20 × 4 × cos 30° = 80 × 0.866 ≈ 69 J. This item tests MCAT-style mechanistic reasoning.
explanation.why_correct: B is correct: approximately 69 J, calculated as W = Fd cos θ = 20 × 4 × cos 30° ≈ 69 J.

wrong_answer_explanations.A: Work is force times displacement in the direction of force regardless of velocity; 0 J is only correct when force is perpendicular to displacement
wrong_answer_explanations.B: This is the correct answer.
wrong_answer_explanations.C: W = Fd only when force is parallel to displacement; the angle must be accounted for with cos θ
wrong_answer_explanations.D: The component of force along the displacement uses cos θ, not sin θ; sin 30° = 0.5 gives 40 J, which is incorrect

explanation.high_yield_takeaway: W = Fd cos θ. Perpendicular force does zero work. Parallel force does maximal work.
explanation.common_trap: Using the full force magnitude without the cosine factor; always project force onto displacement.
explanation.how_to_think: Predict the expected relationship before reading choices, then eliminate those that reverse or overstate it.

passage.title: Circuits Scenario

stem: Three resistors of 6 Ω, 3 Ω, and 2 Ω are connected in parallel. What is the equivalent resistance?

choices.text: 11 Ω, calculated by summing resistances as if in series
2 Ω, by taking only the smallest resistance
3 Ω, by averaging the three resistances

explanation.short: Parallel: 1/Req = Σ(1/Ri). Series: Req = ΣRi. Parallel resistance is always less than the smallest individual resistance.
explanation.detailed: Parallel: 1/Req = Σ(1/Ri). Series: Req = ΣRi. Parallel resistance is always less than the smallest individual resistance. This item tests MCAT-style mechanistic reasoning.
explanation.why_correct: B is correct: 1 Ω, calculated from 1/Req = 1/6 + 1/3 + 1/2 = 1/6 + 2/6 + 3/6 = 6/6 = 1.

wrong_answer_explanations.A: Adding resistances directly applies to series circuits; parallel resistors always yield a lower equivalent resistance than any single branch
wrong_answer_explanations.B: This is the correct answer.
wrong_answer_explanations.C: The equivalent parallel resistance is always less than the smallest branch resistor; taking the minimum directly ignores the other paths
wrong_answer_explanations.D: Averaging has no basis in circuit analysis; the reciprocal formula must be applied

explanation.high_yield_takeaway: Parallel: 1/Req = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + …. Result is always lower than smallest branch.
explanation.common_trap: Adding parallel resistors as if in series (the most common error); parallel adds conductances, not resistances.
explanation.how_to_think: Predict the expected relationship before reading choices, then eliminate those that reverse or overstate it.

passage.text: A study examines fluids using a computational pharmacokinetic model. Investigators are specifically interested in distinguishing undefined from related phenomena.

stem: Blood flows through a wide aorta into a narrower artery. According to the continuity equation, how does velocity change?

choices.text: resistance increases by a factor of 16, because Poiseuille resistance is inversely proportional to radius to the fourth power
resistance increases by a factor of 4, because area decreases by a factor of 4 when radius halves
resistance increases by a factor of 2, because halving the radius doubles the resistance
resistance decreases because a narrower vessel allows faster flow

explanation.short: Poiseuille: R = 8ηL/(πr⁴). Halving r increases R by (1/0.5)⁴ = 2⁴ = 16. Small changes in vessel radius have dramatic effects on resistance.
explanation.detailed: Poiseuille: R = 8ηL/(πr⁴). Halving r increases R by (1/0.5)⁴ = 2⁴ = 16. Small changes in vessel radius have dramatic effects on resistance. This item tests MCAT-style mechanistic reasoning.
explanation.why_correct: A is correct: resistance increases by a factor of 16, because Poiseuille resistance is inversely proportional to radius to the fourth power.

wrong_answer_explanations.A: This is the correct answer.
wrong_answer_explanations.B: The r⁴ relationship is steeper than proportional to area; a factor of 4 would apply to a simple area-based formula
wrong_answer_explanations.C: Resistance scales with r⁻⁴, not r⁻¹; halving r raises resistance by 2⁴ = 16, not 2
wrong_answer_explanations.D: Resistance increases in a narrower vessel; while velocity can increase (continuity), the driving pressure required rises dramatically

explanation.high_yield_takeaway: Poiseuille: R ∝ 1/r⁴. Halving radius → 16× resistance. Continuity: A₁v₁ = A₂v₂.
explanation.common_trap: Using r² (area) instead of r⁴ in Poiseuille's law; the fourth-power dependence is the high-yield fact here.
explanation.how_to_think: Predict the expected relationship before reading choices, then eliminate those that reverse or overstate it.

stem: A converging lens with focal length 10 cm forms an image of an object placed 30 cm from the lens. Which description of the image is correct?

choices.text: no image forms because the object is beyond the focal length
a real, upright image located 30 cm from the lens
a real, inverted, and diminished image located 15 cm from the lens on the far side
a virtual, upright image located 15 cm from the lens on the same side as the object

explanation.short: 1/f = 1/do + 1/di → 1/10 = 1/30 + 1/di → 1/di = 1/10 − 1/30 = 2/30 → di = 15 cm. Positive di = real and inverted.
explanation.detailed: 1/f = 1/do + 1/di → 1/10 = 1/30 + 1/di → 1/di = 1/10 − 1/30 = 2/30 → di = 15 cm. Positive di = real and inverted. This item tests MCAT-style mechanistic reasoning.
explanation.why_correct: C is correct: a real, inverted, and diminished image located 15 cm from the lens on the far side.

wrong_answer_explanations.A: Objects beyond the focal length always produce real images; objects inside the focal length produce virtual images
wrong_answer_explanations.B: Real images formed by converging lenses are always inverted; a real upright image is impossible with a single converging lens
wrong_answer_explanations.C: This is the correct answer.
wrong_answer_explanations.D: Virtual, upright images form only when the object is inside the focal length; here object distance (30 cm) > f (10 cm), so a real image forms

explanation.high_yield_takeaway: Thin lens: 1/f = 1/do + 1/di. Positive di → real, inverted image. Negative di → virtual, upright.
explanation.common_trap: Assuming objects beyond 2f always produce diminished images; use the lens equation to calculate rather than guess.
explanation.how_to_think: Predict the expected relationship before reading choices, then eliminate those that reverse or overstate it.

passage.title: Waves Scenario
passage.text: A study examines waves using a controlled animal model. Investigators are specifically interested in distinguishing undefined from related phenomena.

stem: Two waves of equal amplitude and frequency interfere. One wave is shifted by half a wavelength relative to the other. What is the resultant amplitude?

choices.text: resonance: the truck's frequency matches the observer's natural frequency
the Doppler effect: the observer perceives higher frequency because successive wave crests arrive more frequently as the source approaches
diffraction: sound bends around the observer causing frequency increase
constructive interference: approaching sources always amplify sound

explanation.short: Doppler effect: when source and observer approach, observed frequency f' = f(v+vo)/(v−vs). Moving source approaching → f' > f; receding → f' < f.
explanation.detailed: Doppler effect: when source and observer approach, observed frequency f' = f(v+vo)/(v−vs). Moving source approaching → f' > f; receding → f' < f. This item tests MCAT-style mechanistic reasoning.
explanation.why_correct: B is correct: the Doppler effect: the observer perceives higher frequency because successive wave crests arrive more frequently as the source approaches.

wrong_answer_explanations.A: Resonance requires matching natural frequencies of a resonating body; it does not cause a frequency shift tied to source motion
wrong_answer_explanations.B: This is the correct answer.
wrong_answer_explanations.C: Diffraction is bending of waves around obstacles; it does not shift the perceived frequency
wrong_answer_explanations.D: Constructive interference involves overlapping waves in space, not a moving source; the effect disappears when the truck passes

explanation.high_yield_takeaway: Doppler: approaching source → higher observed frequency. Receding → lower. Half-wavelength shift → destructive interference (amplitude = 0).
explanation.common_trap: Confusing Doppler (frequency shift from motion) with changes in amplitude or resonance phenomena.
explanation.how_to_think: Predict the expected relationship before reading choices, then eliminate those that reverse or overstate it.

stem: A buffer prepared from acetic acid (pKa 4.76) and sodium acetate has pH 5.76. Which ratio of [acetate]/[acetic acid] satisfies the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation?

choices.text: 100:1, because the pH difference from pKa is mistakenly doubled
1:1, because equal concentrations always produce a pH equal to the pKa
10:1 (conjugate base to acid), because pH exceeds pKa by exactly one unit and log(10) = 1
1:10 (acid to base), because the ratio appears inverted when the log term is misread

explanation.short: pH = pKa + log([A−]/[HA]). A pH one unit above pKa requires [A−]/[HA] = 10¹ = 10.
explanation.detailed: pH = pKa + log([A−]/[HA]). A pH one unit above pKa requires [A−]/[HA] = 10¹ = 10. This item tests MCAT-style mechanistic reasoning.
explanation.why_correct: C is correct: 10:1 (conjugate base to acid), because pH exceeds pKa by exactly one unit and log(10) = 1.

wrong_answer_explanations.A: A 100:1 ratio gives pH = pKa + 2; the two-unit shift is double what the question specifies
wrong_answer_explanations.B: Equal concentrations give pH = pKa (log 1 = 0); this ignores the one-unit pH elevation specified
wrong_answer_explanations.C: This is the correct answer.
wrong_answer_explanations.D: A 1:10 ratio gives pH = pKa − 1, not pKa + 1; inverting the base/acid direction reverses the sign of the log term

explanation.high_yield_takeaway: Each pH unit from pKa corresponds to a 10-fold change in [A−]/[HA].
explanation.common_trap: Confusing acid/base direction in the ratio flips the sign and gives the mirror-image wrong answer.
explanation.how_to_think: Predict the expected relationship before reading choices, then eliminate those that reverse or overstate it.

stem: A reaction has ΔH = −80 kJ/mol and ΔS = −200 J/(mol·K). At what temperature does the reaction shift from spontaneous to non-spontaneous?

choices.text: ΔH positive and ΔS positive, which becomes spontaneous at high temperature, not low
ΔH negative and ΔS negative; the unfavorable −TΔS term (positive) overtakes ΔH at high temperature
ΔH positive and ΔS negative, which is never spontaneous at any temperature
ΔH negative and ΔS positive, which is spontaneous at all temperatures

explanation.short: ΔG = ΔH − TΔS. When both terms are negative, ΔG < 0 at low T but the +TΔS term eventually dominates as T rises, making ΔG > 0.
explanation.detailed: ΔG = ΔH − TΔS. When both terms are negative, ΔG < 0 at low T but the +TΔS term eventually dominates as T rises, making ΔG > 0. This item tests MCAT-style mechanistic reasoning.
explanation.why_correct: B is correct: ΔH negative and ΔS negative; the unfavorable −TΔS term (positive) overtakes ΔH at high temperature.

wrong_answer_explanations.A: ΔH+ / ΔS+ reactions become spontaneous as T rises (high-T favorable), the opposite of what's described
wrong_answer_explanations.B: This is the correct answer.
wrong_answer_explanations.C: ΔH+ / ΔS− gives ΔG positive at all temperatures; it cannot be spontaneous at any temperature
wrong_answer_explanations.D: ΔH− / ΔS+ gives ΔG negative at all temperatures; this cannot shift from spontaneous to non-spontaneous

explanation.high_yield_takeaway: Memorize the four ΔH/ΔS sign combinations and their temperature dependence.
explanation.common_trap: Confusing which sign combination is 'always spontaneous' vs 'temperature-dependent' is the most common error.

stem: Nitrogen and hydrogen gases react to form ammonia. Adding more nitrogen to the equilibrium mixture at constant volume and temperature shifts the reaction in which direction?

choices.text: the equilibrium constant Keq increases because higher pressure favors product formation
the equilibrium shifts toward the product side (fewer gas moles) to reduce pressure, consistent with Le Chatelier's principle
the equilibrium shifts toward reactants regardless of the mole ratio of gases
no shift occurs because Keq depends only on temperature, so concentrations are unaffected

explanation.short: Le Chatelier's principle: a system at equilibrium responds to oppose any imposed change. Compression increases pressure, so the reaction shifts toward the side with fewer gas moles to relieve it.
explanation.detailed: Le Chatelier's principle: a system at equilibrium responds to oppose any imposed change. Compression increases pressure, so the reaction shifts toward the side with fewer gas moles to relieve it. This item tests MCAT-style mechanistic reasoning.
explanation.why_correct: B is correct: the equilibrium shifts toward the product side (fewer gas moles) to reduce pressure, consistent with Le Chatelier's principle.

wrong_answer_explanations.A: Keq is a constant at fixed temperature; pressure changes shift the reaction position but never change Keq
wrong_answer_explanations.B: This is the correct answer.
wrong_answer_explanations.C: Le Chatelier predicts the system opposes the disturbance; if products have fewer gas moles, compression favors products, not reactants
wrong_answer_explanations.D: Concentration and pressure changes do shift the equilibrium position; it is Keq that remains constant, not the concentrations

explanation.high_yield_takeaway: Le Chatelier: predict the direction that reduces the applied stress. Keq changes only with temperature.
explanation.common_trap: Students confuse 'Keq does not change' with 'nothing happens.' Reactant and product concentrations shift even though Keq stays the same.
explanation.how_to_think: Predict the expected relationship before reading choices, then eliminate those that reverse or overstate it.

the zinc electrode is the anode because zinc is oxidized (loses electrons), which drives the spontaneous cell

stem: The Nernst equation predicts how cell potential changes as a reaction proceeds. At equilibrium, which value does Q equal?

choices.text: E > E°cell because when Q < 1 the reaction quotient term (−RT/nF × ln Q) is positive, adding to E°
E is undefined when Q departs from 1
E = E°cell because Q < 1 has no effect until equilibrium
E < E°cell because non-standard conditions always reduce the driving force

explanation.short: Nernst equation: E = E° − (RT/nF)ln Q. When Q < 1, ln Q < 0, so the subtracted term becomes negative, raising E above E°.
explanation.detailed: Nernst equation: E = E° − (RT/nF)ln Q. When Q < 1, ln Q < 0, so the subtracted term becomes negative, raising E above E°. This item tests MCAT-style mechanistic reasoning.
explanation.why_correct: A is correct: E > E°cell because when Q < 1 the reaction quotient term (−RT/nF × ln Q) is positive, adding to E°.

wrong_answer_explanations.A: This is the correct answer.
wrong_answer_explanations.B: The Nernst equation applies at any Q; it is well-defined for all positive Q values
wrong_answer_explanations.C: Q < 1 means products are low relative to reactants, increasing the driving force and raising E above E°
wrong_answer_explanations.D: Non-standard E can be higher than E° when Q < 1; the assumption that it is always lower ignores the log term's sign

explanation.high_yield_takeaway: Q < 1 → E > E°. Q > 1 → E < E°. Q = Keq → E = 0 (equilibrium).
explanation.common_trap: Students assume non-standard always means lower potential; direction depends on whether Q < 1 or Q > 1.
explanation.how_to_think: Predict the expected relationship before reading choices, then eliminate those that reverse or overstate it.

stem: A mixture of H2 (M = 2) and O2 (M = 32) effuses through a small opening. Which gas effuses faster and by what factor?

choices.text: O2 effuses faster because it has more mass and therefore more momentum
H2 effuses 4 times faster than O2 because rate is inversely proportional to the square root of molar mass
both gases effuse at the same rate because temperature determines kinetic energy equally
H2 effuses twice as fast because its molar mass is half that of O2

explanation.short: Graham's law: rate ∝ 1/√M. Rate(H2)/Rate(O2) = √(32/2) = √16 = 4.
explanation.detailed: Graham's law: rate ∝ 1/√M. Rate(H2)/Rate(O2) = √(32/2) = √16 = 4. This item tests MCAT-style mechanistic reasoning.
explanation.why_correct: B is correct: H2 effuses 4 times faster than O2 because rate is inversely proportional to the square root of molar mass.

wrong_answer_explanations.A: Graham's law gives rate ∝ 1/√M; heavier gas is slower, not faster, regardless of momentum
wrong_answer_explanations.B: This is the correct answer.
wrong_answer_explanations.C: Temperature equalizes average kinetic energy but not speed; lighter molecules move faster at the same KE
wrong_answer_explanations.D: H2/O2 molar mass ratio is 1/16, so rate ratio = √16 = 4, not 2; square root is required

explanation.high_yield_takeaway: Graham's law: ratio of rates = square root of the inverse molar mass ratio.
explanation.common_trap: Students use the molar mass ratio directly rather than its square root.
explanation.how_to_think: Predict the expected relationship before reading choices, then eliminate those that reverse or overstate it.

stem: A primary alkyl bromide reacts with sodium cyanide (strong nucleophile) in acetone. Which mechanism and stereochemical outcome are most expected?

choices.text: SN2 with inversion of configuration, because the primary substrate is unhindered and the strong nucleophile performs backside attack
E2 elimination because cyanide is too bulky to reach the backside
SN1 with racemization, because the primary substrate forms a stable primary carbocation that is attacked from both faces
No reaction because primary substrates are too stable for nucleophilic substitution

explanation.short: SN2: strong nucleophile + primary (or methyl) substrate + polar aprotic solvent → inversion. SN1: weak nucleophile or solvolysis + tertiary substrate + polar protic solvent → racemization.
explanation.detailed: SN2: strong nucleophile + primary (or methyl) substrate + polar aprotic solvent → inversion. SN1: weak nucleophile or solvolysis + tertiary substrate + polar protic solvent → racemization. This item tests MCAT-style mechanistic reasoning.
explanation.why_correct: A is correct: SN2 with inversion of configuration, because the primary substrate is unhindered and the strong nucleophile performs backside attack.

wrong_answer_explanations.A: This is the correct answer.
wrong_answer_explanations.B: Cyanide is a linear, compact anion and is not sterically hindered; bulky bases favor elimination but cyanide is not bulky
wrong_answer_explanations.C: Primary carbocations are highly unstable and do not form under normal conditions; SN1 requires at least secondary (preferably tertiary) substrates
wrong_answer_explanations.D: Primary substrates are among the most reactive in SN2 due to minimal steric hindrance; they do react readily

explanation.high_yield_takeaway: SN2: primary, strong Nu, polar aprotic, inversion. SN1: tertiary, weak Nu, polar protic, racemization.
explanation.common_trap: Students default to SN1 for any substrate; remember primary substrates cannot form stable carbocations.
explanation.how_to_think: Predict the expected relationship before reading choices, then eliminate those that reverse or overstate it.

stem: An aldehyde is treated with excess sodium borohydride (NaBH4) in methanol. What is the primary product?

a carboxylic acid, because NaBH4 oxidizes aldehydes in the presence of base

stem: An IR spectrum shows a broad absorption centered near 3300 cm−1 and a sharp absorption at 1715 cm−1. Which functional groups are most consistent with these peaks?

choices.text: an alkyne C≡C (~2100–2260 cm−1) and an alcohol O–H (~3300 cm−1)
an alcohol O–H (broad 3200–3550 cm−1) and a carbonyl C=O (sharp ~1715 cm−1)
an aldehyde C–H (two weak peaks ~2700–2850 cm−1) and a C–O ether stretch (~1100 cm−1)
an amine N–H (sharp doublet ~3300–3500 cm−1) and an alkene C=C (~1640 cm−1)

explanation.short: Broad O–H: 3200–3550 cm−1 (alcohol) or 2500–3300 cm−1 (carboxylic acid). Carbonyl C=O: ~1715 cm−1 (ketone/acid), ~1735 cm−1 (ester), ~1670 cm−1 (amide). Aldehyde C–H: ~2720 and 2820 cm−1.
explanation.detailed: Broad O–H: 3200–3550 cm−1 (alcohol) or 2500–3300 cm−1 (carboxylic acid). Carbonyl C=O: ~1715 cm−1 (ketone/acid), ~1735 cm−1 (ester), ~1670 cm−1 (amide). Aldehyde C–H: ~2720 and 2820 cm−1. This item tests MCAT-style mechanistic reasoning.
explanation.why_correct: B is correct: an alcohol O–H (broad 3200–3550 cm−1) and a carbonyl C=O (sharp ~1715 cm−1).

wrong_answer_explanations.A: Alkyne triple bond absorbs ~2100–2260 cm−1; the 1715 cm−1 carbonyl is inconsistent with this pairing
wrong_answer_explanations.B: This is the correct answer.
wrong_answer_explanations.C: Aldehyde C–H appears as two weak peaks near 2700–2850 cm−1, not a broad 3300 cm−1 absorption; ether C–O is ~1100 cm−1, not 1715
wrong_answer_explanations.D: Amine N–H appears as a sharp doublet (primary) or singlet (secondary), not a broad single peak; alkene C=C absorbs ~1640 cm−1, not 1715 cm−1

explanation.high_yield_takeaway: Broad O–H ~3300 = alcohol. Carbonyl ~1715 = ketone or acid. Aldehyde: two weak C–H peaks ~2700–2850.
explanation.common_trap: Mistaking the aldehyde C–H doublet for alcohol O–H; aldehyde peak is weak and appears as two peaks, not a broad hump.
